skill.name: threejs-performance
skill.description: Measuring and optimizing three.js speed: render statistics, memory counters, fewer draw calls via merging, instancing, batching and LOD, fill rate, shadows, CPU work per frame, shader stalls and GPU compute for particles, WebGL or WebGPU with TSL. Use when a scene is slow, janks or exceeds memory.
skill.summary: Profile Three.js scenes and reduce rendering, memory, and animation costs in WebGL and WebGPU.
skill.author: cloudai-x

content.value_statement: Slow Three.js scenes can have several causes, and frame rate alone does not identify them. Use renderer counters and browser profiles to prioritize fixes.
actual_capabilities: Explain how to collect and interpret draw calls, triangle counts, GPU resource counters, and frame timings.
Compare geometry merging, instancing, batching, and level of detail for different scene layouts.
Estimate texture memory from dimensions and format, and explain compression and resource disposal.
Identify rendering costs from pixel ratio, transparent layers, and shadow maps.
Suggest ways to reduce raycasting, repeated matrix updates, per-frame allocations, and shader compilation stalls.
Show how a WebGPU compute pass can update particle positions in a GPU storage buffer with TSL.
limitations: The examples target Three.js r186. Check API availability if your project uses another release.
This guide does not collect benchmarks. Run the scene on target devices to measure the effect of changes.
WebGL resource counts are not byte totals. WebGPU memory estimates can understate compressed texture usage.
WebGPU compute and some batching benefits depend on the browser, device, and renderer backend.

use_cases.title: Set scenery budgets
use_cases.description: Choose where to instance repeated assets, merge static objects, or use lower detail at a distance.

use_cases.title: Evaluate WebGPU particles
use_cases.description: Compare a CPU particle update with a TSL compute pass and define what to measure on supported hardware.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the first counters
prompt_templates.prompt: My Three.js WebGL scene stutters while rotating the camera. Which counters should I collect after rendering, and what does each one tell me?

prompt_templates.title: Reduce draws for repeated meshes
prompt_templates.prompt: My scene has 500 identical trees. Compare instancing and clustered merging, and suggest how to measure the effect of culling.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate memory growth
prompt_templates.prompt: Texture counts grow after repeated scene swaps. Review my cleanup code and identify where shared resources need ownership checks before disposal.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a WebGPU compute comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my CPU particle loop and outline a TSL compute alternative using a GPU storage buffer. Propose a benchmark that separates CPU time, frame time, and renderer counters.

output_examples.input: Frame time increases when I raise the pixel ratio, but draw calls are unchanged.
output_examples.output: Extra pixel work is a likely cause. Test a lower pixel ratio with the same camera path and compare frame times and visual quality.

output_examples.input: Tree rendering still costs time when most trees are offscreen.
output_examples.output: A single instanced mesh uses one shared culling bound. Try spatial clusters and compare draw calls and frame times from the same viewpoints.

output_examples.input: The first appearance of a material causes a visible pause.
output_examples.output: Test asynchronous shader compilation during loading. Measure the first visible frame separately because shadow shaders may still compile on their first use.

best_practices: Use the same camera path, device, and render settings for baseline and comparison runs.
Measure several frames and track CPU time separately from elapsed frame time.
Confirm that no live mesh uses a shared geometry, material, or texture before disposing of it.
anti_patterns: Reading WebGL draw counters before rendering and treating them as current frame measurements.
Merging an entire level into one mesh without checking the loss of culling precision.
Using a WebGL texture count as a measurement of GPU memory in bytes.

faq.question: Which Three.js release does the guide target?
faq.answer: The examples target r186. Most examples use WebGLRenderer, and the WebGPU and TSL examples use WebGPURenderer.

faq.question: Can the skill find my bottleneck without a trace?
faq.answer: It can suggest what to measure from your code and symptoms. A browser profile or controlled comparison is needed to confirm the bottleneck.

faq.question: How do I count draws across multiple WebGL passes?
faq.answer: Disable automatic counter resets, render all passes, read the accumulated counters, and reset once after the final pass.

faq.question: When should I use instancing rather than batching?
faq.answer: Use instancing for repeated geometry with a shared material. Consider batching for different geometries that share a material, and check your backend for draw call savings.

faq.question: Does removing a mesh free its textures?
faq.answer: No. Dispose of textures separately when nothing still uses them.

faq.question: Can draw counts reveal the cost of transparency?
faq.answer: They can reveal extra passes, but not how many pixels overlapping layers shade. Compare frame times with and without the transparent layers.
